The Respondent, PSPCL, has submitted that the claim arises out of a contractual dispute relating to works awarded in the year 2005, under the original scope of the Uri-II project. Respondent PSPCL has further submitted that the Petitioner has not furnished adequate documentary evidence substantiating the 116. The Respondents, BRPL and BYPL, vide their affidavit, have also opposed the recovery of water cess and have submitted that in the absence of adequate steps undertaken by the Petitioner to mitigate the impact of the disputed water cess, the in this order (after truing up exercise) for the period 2019-24 in respect of the - _(d) Payment against the award of arbitration or for compliance with the directions or order of any statutory authority or order or decree of any court of law;_ 136. The Petitioner has submitted claims under Regulation 25(1)(a) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, with respect to payments arising out of the following Arbitration/Court cases against disputes with M/s Hindustan Construction Company (“HCC”) during the period 2024-29. These are examined in the subsequent paragraphs. 147. Respondents, RUVNL, BRPL and BYPL, in their affidavit submitted that the payments in compliance with the Arbitral Award were made in the year 2018-19 and no claim was made by the Petitioner in the earlier petitions, in order to reimburse arbitral interest or allow notional interest, thereby making the said claim time-barred. 153. The Petitioner, in its rejoinder, has clarified that its claim for principal and interest is admissible under Regulation 25(1)(a) and Regulation 91 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, respectively, as payment to M/s HCC was made pursuant to the Arbitral Award and in mandatory compliance with the directives of NITI Aayog. Further, the Petitioner submitted that the liability is recognised and capitalised in its audited accounts. 157. In view of the same, we have admitted the principal amount paid by the Petitioner along with any discharges against liability corresponding to the disputes as part of additional capital expenditure under Regulations 25(1)(a) of the 2024 Tariff 158. Further, we have considered the claims of the Petitioner with respect to the interest amount paid to the contractor, i.e., M/s HCC and allow recovery of the same in accordance with Regulation 91 of the Tariff Regulations, 2024, in twelve monthly instalments from the beneficiaries.
